title: The Forgotten Wolf
premise: Felix Thackeray keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things and guards the Hollow Gate, a door that trades in memories the world would rather lose. When the crown declares a hunt for anyone bearing the gift of unbinding, Felix is dragged into it because the king himself is bound—possessed by the thing wearing his crown, a hunger that eats memories to stay alive. To save him, Felix must reopen the Hollow Gate and trade away the memories she loves most, including her love for the king's exiled brother, Aldous. In the end she unbinds the king at the cost of forgetting Aldous entirely, and the final chapter turns on whether love can survive being remembered by only one person.
about_author: Bram Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters no one ever claimed. They write fantasies about doors, debts, and the people who keep both.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She balances the guild's ledgers, records a trade of a shadow for a name, and quietly guards the Hollow Gate. Her careful, wry voice establishes the world's rules: everything traded costs memory. Beat: contentment built on routine, with a hairline crack—the gate has been whispering her name at night.

chapters.title: A Proclamation in Ash
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Crown criers announce the Unbinding Hunt: anyone with the gift will be taken. A guild courier arrives burned and half-mad, carrying a page torn from the royal ledger—evidence the king himself is bound. Beat: dread; Felix realizes the guild's neutrality is over.

chapters.title: The Brother in Exile
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with a flashback to Aldous. Aldous Thackeray, the king's exiled brother, comes to the guild seeking sanctuary and forces Felix to admit the torn page is her own hand's work from years ago—she bound the king once, as an apprentice, believing she was healing him. Beat: guilt and the first spark of old love rekindled.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV. The pair infiltrate the capital's memory-archive beneath the palace. They learn the thing wearing the crown is the Hunger, a parasite that eats the king's memories to survive, and that it is nearly full—when the king forgets his own name, it will rule outright. Beat: rising stakes, ticking clock established.

chapters.title: The Hunt Finds Her
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The king's inquisitor, Mistress Vane, raids the guild. Felix burns the ledgers to protect the traders' names and flees through the Hollow Gate itself, emerging somewhere impossible: the guild's founding, forty years ago. Beat: terror transformed into awe; the gate is a door in time, not just space.

chapters.title: The Apprentice I Was
chapters.summary: Felix's POV in the past. She meets her younger self and the guild's founder, learning the terrible truth: the Hunger was invited in by the founder, and the binding Felix made as an apprentice didn't imprison it—it fed it, keeping it patient. Beat: devastating reversal; she caused the crisis she must now solve.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Aldous's POV, parallel timeline. Aldous lets himself be captured by Vane to buy Felix time, trading his own memories of her to the archive in exchange for the unbinding rite. Beat: love against duty—his sacrifice made without her knowledge, so she cannot refuse it.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. She returns through the gate to a guild in ruins and finds Aldous hollowed, no longer remembering her. In the throne room she begins the rite as the king's mind frays. The Hunger offers her a trade: the king's life for her memories of Aldous. Beat: climax of choice; she accepts.

chapters.title: The King and the Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The unbinding succeeds; the king wakes whole and orders the Hunt ended, but Felix cannot remember why she is crying, why Aldous's name is written in her own hand across every surviving ledger page. Beat: grief without an object; justice won, memory lost.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Forgot
chapters.summary: Aldous and Felix, alternating. Aldous remembers everything and chooses not to tell her, instead courting her again from the beginning. In the last scene, Felix finds a ledger entry in her own handwriting: 'If you are reading this, love him anyway.' She closes the book and opens the door. Beat: bittersweet hope; memory ends, love restarts.
